ment-result-means.meaning: result or means of an action

ate-make-act.meaning: to make or act on; having

burs-bursa-fluid.zh: 滑囊（关节处含液体的囊）

thromb-blood-clot.meaning: a blood clot, clotting of blood

my-muscle.story: A flexing muscle looked like a mouse moving under the skin: Greek mûs means both mouse and muscle, and Latin musculus, our "muscle", means "little mouse".
my-muscle.zh: 肌肉收缩时，样子像一只老鼠在皮下移动：希腊语 mûs 既指“老鼠”，也指“肌肉”；英语 muscle 所源自的拉丁语 musculus 意为“小老鼠”。

cand-glowing-iridescent.story: Roman candidates for office wore a toga whitened with chalk, the toga candida, so a candidate is literally "one dressed in white".
cand-glowing-iridescent.zh: 古罗马竞选公职的人穿着用白垩染白的托加袍，称为 toga candida。因此，candidate 的字面意思是“身穿白衣的人”。

chol-bile.story: Melancholy is "black bile": ancient medicine blamed sadness on an excess of it, one of the four humours.
chol-bile.zh: Melancholy 的字面意思是“黑胆汁”。古代医学曾把悲伤归因于黑胆汁过多；黑胆汁是当时所谓“四体液”之一。这是历史观念。

electr-amber-hence.story: Rubbed amber attracts light objects. In 1600 William Gilbert coined Latin electricus, "like amber", for the effect, from Greek ēlektron, "amber".
electr-amber-hence.zh: 摩擦后的琥珀能吸引轻小物体。1600 年，威廉·吉尔伯特用希腊语 ēlektron（琥珀）造出拉丁语 electricus（像琥珀的），来描述这种现象。

pan-bread.story: A companion is someone you share bread with (com- "with" + panis "bread").
pan-bread.zh: Companion 指“一起分享面包的人”：com- 表示“一起”，panis 表示“面包”。

sarc-flesh.story: Sarcasm comes from Greek sarkazein, from sarx "flesh": "to tear flesh", or to gnash the teeth in anger. A sarcophagus is a "flesh-eater": the limestone was believed to consume the bodies laid in it.
sarc-flesh.zh: Sarcasm 来自希腊语 sarkazein，源于 sarx（肉），意为“撕肉”，也指愤怒地咬牙。Sarcophagus（石棺）的字面意思是“食肉者”：当时人们认为，制棺的石灰岩会消蚀放在里面的尸体。

vi-way.story: Trivial comes from trivium, a place where three roads meet, and so something ordinary or commonplace.
vi-way.zh: Trivial 来自 trivium（三条道路交汇之处），由此引申为“普通的、平常的”。

aster-star-star.story: A disaster is literally a "bad star": misfortune was once blamed on an unfavourable position of the planets.
aster-star-star.zh: Disaster 的字面意思是“不好的星”。过去，人们曾把灾祸归咎于不利的星体位置。

idi-own-peculiarity.story: An idiot was originally a "private person", a layman who took no part in public life (Greek idiōtēs).
idi-own-peculiarity.zh: Idiot 最初指“私人、普通人”，即不参与公共生活的外行人，来自希腊语 idiōtēs。

lun-moon.story: Lunatic reflects the old belief that madness came and went with the phases of the moon.
lun-moon.zh: Lunatic 反映了旧时的一种观念：人们以为精神失常会随月相变化而出现或消退。

noc-hurt-harm.zh: Innocent 的字面意思是“不伤害”：in- 表示“不”，nocere 表示“伤害”。

vill-country-house.story: A villain was originally a farm labourer on a villa, a country estate. The meaning slid from "peasant" to "scoundrel" through upper-class contempt.
vill-country-house.zh: Villain 最初指在 villa（乡间庄园）劳作的农人。由于上层阶级的轻蔑，这个词逐渐从“农民”变成了“恶棍”。

dent-teeth.story: The dandelion is named for its jagged leaves: French dent de lion, "lion's tooth".
dent-teeth.zh: Dandelion（蒲公英）因锯齿状叶片得名：法语 dent de lion 意为“狮子的牙齿”。

capit-head.story: Wealth was once counted in head of livestock, which is why "cattle" and "chattel" both come from Latin capitale, from caput "head", as does capital.
capit-head.zh: 过去，人们按牲畜的“头数”计算财富。因此，cattle（牛）和 chattel（动产）都来自拉丁语 capitale，再追溯到 caput（头）；capital 也同源。

hyster-womb-uterus.story: Hysteria was named in the belief that it was caused by a disturbance of the womb.
hyster-womb-uterus.zh: Hysteria 的命名源于当时的一种误解：人们认为这种病症是由子宫的异常造成的。

vacc-cow.story: Edward Jenner protected people against smallpox with cowpox (variolae vaccinae, "cow pox"), which gave us the word vaccine.
vacc-cow.zh: 爱德华·詹纳用牛痘预防天花。牛痘的拉丁语名称是 variolae vaccinae，英语 vaccine（疫苗）由此得名。

calc-calcium-stone.story: Romans counted with small pebbles, calculi, which gave us calculate. Doctors still call kidney stones calculi.
calc-calcium-stone.zh: 古罗马人用小石子 calculi 计数，英语 calculate 因此得名。医学中现在仍把结石称为 calculi。

mon-warn.story: A monster was originally a monstrum, a divine omen or warning, from monere, "to warn".
mon-warn.zh: Monster 最初是拉丁语 monstrum，指神示的征兆或警告，源于 monere（警告）。

bibl-book.story: Greek biblos, "papyrus, book", is named after Byblos, the Phoenician port that exported papyrus to Greece.
bibl-book.zh: 希腊语 biblos 表示“纸莎草、书”，得名于腓尼基港口比布鲁斯（Byblos）；该港曾向希腊出口纸莎草。

gymn-nude.story: Greek athletes trained naked, so a gymnasium was literally a "place for exercising naked".
gymn-nude.zh: 古希腊运动员裸体训练，因此 gymnasium 的字面意思是“裸体锻炼的场所”。

paed-child.story: A pedagogue was a slave who walked children to school. An encyclopedia comes from Greek enkyklios paideia, "all-round education".
paed-child.zh: Pedagogue 最初指陪孩子步行上学的奴隶。Encyclopedia 则来自希腊语 enkyklios paideia，意为“全面的教育”。

naut-ship.story: Nausea comes from Greek naus, "ship": it first meant seasickness.
naut-ship.zh: Nausea 来自希腊语 naus（船），最初的意思是“晕船”。

hol-whole.story: A holocaust was originally a sacrifice "burnt whole" (Greek holos + kaustos).
hol-whole.zh: Holocaust 最初指“完全焚烧的祭品”，由希腊语 holos（整个）和 kaustos（烧过的）组成。

cosm-universe.story: Greek kosmos meant "order" and also "ornament", which is why the universe (an ordered whole) and cosmetics share a root.
cosm-universe.zh: 希腊语 kosmos 既表示“秩序”，也表示“装饰”。所以，表示有序整体的“宇宙”和 cosmetics（化妆品）共享这个词根。

clin-lean-recline.story: Clinic comes from the related Greek klinē, "bed": clinical medicine was taught at the patient's bedside.
clin-lean-recline.zh: Clinic 来自相关的希腊语 klinē（床）；临床医学过去是在病人床边教授的。

crit-judge-separate.story: A hypocrite was originally a stage actor, Greek hypokritēs: someone playing a part.
crit-judge-separate.zh: Hypocrite 最初指舞台演员，来自希腊语 hypokritēs，即“扮演角色的人”。

dyna-power.story: Alfred Nobel named his invention dynamite from Greek dynamis, "power". His fortune from it later funded the Nobel Prizes.
dyna-power.zh: 阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔用希腊语 dynamis（力量）为他的发明命名：dynamite（炸药）。后来，他的财富被用于设立诺贝尔奖。

avi-bird.story: Roman priests foretold the future by watching birds, so something auspicious was literally "bird-watched" and found favourable (avis + specere).
avi-bird.zh: 古罗马祭司通过观察鸟来占卜。因此，auspicious 最初指“观鸟占卜后发现吉兆的”，由 avis（鸟）和 specere（看）组成。

vir-man.story: Virtue first meant "manliness" or valour, from Latin vir, "man".
vir-man.zh: Virtue 最初表示“男子气概”或“勇武”，来自拉丁语 vir（男人）。

vir-poison-venom.story: Latin virus meant "poison" or "slimy liquid" long before anyone could see the particles we now call viruses.
vir-poison-venom.zh: 在人类能够看见今天所说的病毒颗粒之前很久，拉丁语 virus 就已经表示“毒物”或“黏液”。

greg-flock-herd.story: Egregious means "out of the flock". It first meant "outstanding" in a good way, and only later took on its bad sense.
greg-flock-herd.zh: Egregious 的字面意思是“出众于群”。它起初是褒义的“杰出”，后来才有了贬义。

cor-heart.story: To record is literally to "bring back to the heart": Latin recordari, "to remember". We still learn things "by heart".
cor-heart.zh: Record 的字面意思是“带回心中”：拉丁语 recordari 表示“记起”。英语现在仍用 learn by heart 表示“熟记”。

mort-death.story: A mortgage is literally a "dead pledge" (Old French mort gage, translating Medieval Latin mortuum vadium).
mort-death.zh: Mortgage 的字面意思是“死的抵押”，来自古法语 mort gage，是对中世纪拉丁语 mortuum vadium 的翻译。

ped-foot.story: Pedigree comes from French pied de grue, "crane's foot", after the branching lines on family-tree charts.
ped-foot.zh: Pedigree 来自法语 pied de grue（鹤脚），得名于家谱图上像鹤脚一样分叉的线条。

cad-fall.story: The Occident (the West) is where the sun "falls", from occidere, "to fall, set".
cad-fall.zh: Occident（西方）是太阳“落下”的地方，来自 occidere（落下、日落）。

ori-rise.story: The Orient (the East) is where the sun rises, from oriri, "to rise".
ori-rise.zh: Orient（东方）是太阳升起的地方，来自 oriri（升起）。

sci-know.story: "Nice" comes from Latin nescius, "not knowing", and once meant foolish before drifting to its modern sense.
sci-know.zh: Nice 来自拉丁语 nescius（不知道的）。它一度表示“愚蠢”，后来才逐渐演变为现代含义。

sed-sit.story: A president is literally "one who sits in front", presiding over a meeting.
sed-sit.zh: President 的字面意思是“坐在前面的人”，即主持会议的人。

cap-hold-take.story: Recipe is Latin for "take!": the first word of a doctor's prescription, later used for cooking instructions.
cap-hold-take.zh: Recipe 在拉丁语中是命令式的“取用！”，原本是医生处方的开头，后来也用于烹饪说明。

sol-sun.story: The solstice is when the sun seems to "stand still" (sol + sistere) before its path turns back.
sol-sun.zh: Solstice（至日）是太阳在运行轨迹折返之前看似“停住”的时候：sol 表示“太阳”，sistere 表示“使站住”。

sec-cut.story: An insect is "cut into" segments: a Latin translation of Greek entomon, which gives us entomology.
sec-cut.zh: Insect 指身体被“切分”成节的生物，是对希腊语 entomon 的拉丁语翻译；entomology（昆虫学）也来自这个希腊词。

tem-cut.story: An atom is literally "uncuttable", the smallest possible piece. Atoms were later split anyway.
tem-cut.zh: Atom 的字面意思是“不可切分的”，即最小的单位。尽管如此，人类后来仍然分裂了原子。

eco-house-household.zh: Economy 最初表示“家务管理”：希腊语 oikos 表示“家”，nemein 表示“管理、分配”。

arch-ruler-chief.zh: Architect 的字面意思是“首席建造者”：希腊语 arkhi- 表示“首席”，tektōn 表示“建造者”。

dem-people.story: An epidemic is a disease "upon the people", spreading through a population.
dem-people.zh: Epidemic 指疾病“在人群之上”，也就是在人群中传播。

phil-love-friendship.story: Philadelphia, "the city of brotherly love", is Greek philos "loving" + adelphos "brother".
phil-love-friendship.zh: Philadelphia（费城）意为“兄弟之爱的城市”，由希腊语 philos（爱的）和 adelphos（兄弟）组成。

tele-far-at.story: Television mixes Greek tele with Latin visio, and early critics complained that the hybrid word was bad Greek and bad Latin.
tele-far-at.zh: Television 混用了希腊语 tele 和拉丁语 visio。早期批评者曾抱怨，这种混合词既不是好希腊语，也不是好拉丁语。

hydr-water.zh: Hydrogen 的意思是“造水者”：氢燃烧会产生水。

oxy-sharp-acid.story: Lavoisier named oxygen "acid-maker" because he wrongly believed every acid contained it.
oxy-sharp-acid.zh: 拉瓦锡把 oxygen 命名为“造酸者”，因为他错误地认为所有酸都含有氧。

mor-foolish-dull.zh: Oxymoron 的字面意思是“尖锐—迟钝”；这个名称本身就是一个矛盾修辞。

fa-say-speak.story: An infant is literally "not speaking", from in- + fari, "to speak".
fa-say-speak.zh: Infant 的字面意思是“不会说话的”，由 in-（不）和 fari（说话）组成。

spir-breathe.story: Spirit first meant "breath". To inspire was to breathe life (or an idea) into someone.
spir-breathe.zh: Spirit 最初表示“呼吸”。Inspire 曾表示“向某人注入生命或想法”，就像吹入一口气。

fil-thread.story: A file was originally a string or wire on which papers were hung to keep them in order (filum, "thread").
fil-thread.zh: File 最初指用来串起文件、使其有序的线或金属丝，来自 filum（线）。

can-dog.story: The Canary Islands were named Insula Canaria, "Island of Dogs", and the birds are named after the islands.
can-dog.zh: 加那利群岛曾被称为 Insula Canaria，意为“犬岛”；canary（金丝雀）则是根据群岛得名的。

vers-turn.story: A verse is a "turning", like a plough turning at the end of a row to start the next line.
vers-turn.zh: Verse 原意是“转弯”，就像犁耕到田垄尽头，转向下一行。

pen-almost.zh: Peninsula 的意思是“几乎是岛”，由 paene（几乎）和 insula（岛）组成。

insul-island.story: Insulin is named after the islets of Langerhans, the "little islands" of cells in the pancreas that make it.
insul-island.zh: Insulin 得名于胰腺中的朗格汉斯岛（胰岛），即产生胰岛素的“小岛状”细胞群。

carn-flesh.story: Carnival possibly comes from Italian carnevale, "removing meat": the feast before the meatless days of Lent. Other origins have been proposed.
carn-flesh.zh: Carnival 可能来自意大利语 carnevale（去掉肉），指大斋期禁肉之前的节庆。不过，也有人提出其他词源解释。

medi-middle.story: The Mediterranean is the sea "in the middle of the land" (medius + terra).
medi-middle.zh: Mediterranean 是“陆地中间的海”，由 medius（中间）和 terra（土地）组成。

alb-white.story: In Rome an album was a white tablet on which public notices were written.
alb-white.zh: 在古罗马，album 指用来书写公告的白色板子。

dexter-right-hand.story: Latin sinister meant "left": the left side was considered unlucky, while dexterity comes from the right hand.
dexter-right-hand.zh: 拉丁语 sinister 表示“左边”；当时左侧被认为不吉利。与之相对，dexterity（灵巧）来自“右手”。

ambi-both-on.story: Ambition comes from ambire, "to go around": Roman candidates went around canvassing for votes.
ambi-both-on.zh: Ambition 来自 ambire（四处走动）：古罗马的候选人四处奔走拉票。

mon-alone-only.story: A monk is "one who lives alone", from Greek monachos, "solitary".
mon-alone-only.zh: Monk 指“独居者”，来自希腊语 monachos（独自的）。

pater-father.zh: Patriot 热爱的是 patria，即“祖国”，字面为“父辈之国”。

cur-care-for.story: A sinecure is a job "without care", that pays without real duties. It was first a church post with no souls to care for.
cur-care-for.zh: Sinecure 是“无需操心”的职位，即领取报酬却没有实际职责的闲职。它最初指没有牧灵职责的教会职位。

sangui-blood.story: Sanguine means hopeful: blood was the humour believed to make people cheerful.
sangui-blood.zh: Sanguine 表示“乐观的”。古代体液学说认为，血液会使人性情开朗。

mal-bad-wretched.story: Malaria is Italian mala aria, "bad air": the disease was blamed on swamp air before mosquitoes were understood.
mal-bad-wretched.zh: Malaria 来自意大利语 mala aria（坏空气）。在人们了解蚊子的传播作用之前，疟疾曾被归咎于沼泽空气。

strat-army.zh: Strategy 的字面意思是“统帅之术”，来自希腊语 stratēgos（军队的领导者）。

cidal-killing-destroying.story: Raphael Lemkin coined "genocide" in 1944 from Greek genos "race" and Latin -cidium "killing".
cidal-killing-destroying.zh: 拉斐尔·莱姆金于 1944 年用希腊语 genos（种族）和拉丁语 -cidium（杀害）造出 genocide（种族灭绝）一词。

ops-eye.story: An autopsy is literally "seeing for oneself" (Greek autos + opsis).
ops-eye.zh: Autopsy 的字面意思是“亲自看”，由希腊语 autos（自己）和 opsis（看）组成。

bi-two-twice.story: A biscuit is literally "twice cooked" (French bis cuit).
bi-two-twice.zh: Biscuit 的字面意思是“烤过两次”，来自法语 bis cuit。

pre-before.zh: Preposterous 的字面意思是“前—后”，由 prae 和 posterus 组成，表示“前后颠倒”。

oct-eight.story: October was the eighth month in the old Roman calendar, which began in March. The same goes for September (seven), November (nine) and December (ten).
oct-eight.zh: 在以三月为年初的古罗马历法中，October 是第八个月。September（七）、November（九）和 December（十）的名称也有相同背景。

dec-ten-tenth.story: To decimate first meant to kill one soldier in ten, a Roman punishment for mutiny.
dec-ten-tenth.zh: Decimate 最初指“每十名士兵处死一名”，是古罗马惩罚兵变的一种方式。

quint-five-fifth.story: Quintessence is the "fifth essence": the ether that ancient philosophers believed filled the heavens, beyond the four elements of earth, water, air and fire.
quint-five-fifth.zh: Quintessence 是“第五种本质”：古代哲学家认为，除了土、水、气、火四种元素，天界还充满第五种元素“以太”。

luc-bright-light.story: Lucifer means "light-bearer" (lux + ferre) and was originally a name for the morning star, Venus.
luc-bright-light.zh: Lucifer 意为“带来光的人”，由 lux（光）和 ferre（携带）组成，最初是晨星（金星）的名称。

ver-true.story: A verdict is literally a "true saying" (vere dictum).
ver-true.zh: Verdict 的字面意思是“真实的话”，来自 vere dictum。

biography.definition_zh: 传记；对某人生平的记述

autobiography.definition: an account of a person's life written by that person
autobiography.definition_zh: 自传；本人撰写的生平记述

telescope.definition: an instrument for seeing distant objects
telescope.definition_zh: 望远镜；观察远处物体的仪器

microscope.definition: an instrument for seeing very small objects
microscope.definition_zh: 显微镜；观察微小物体的仪器

philanthropy.definition: giving money or help to improve other people's lives
philanthropy.definition_zh: 慈善；捐助金钱或提供帮助以改善他人的生活

democracy.definition: government by the people or their elected representatives
democracy.definition_zh: 民主；由人民或其选出的代表治理

autonomy.definition: the right or ability to govern oneself
autonomy.definition_zh: 自治；自我治理的权利或能力

synchronize.definition: to make things happen at the same time
synchronize.definition_zh: 使同步；使事情同时发生

chronology.definition: the order in which events happened

hydrophobia.definition: fear of water; also an old name for rabies, which makes swallowing painful
hydrophobia.definition_zh: 恐水；也曾用来指吞咽疼痛的狂犬病

transport.definition: to move from one place to another
transport.definition_zh: 运输；从一处移到另一处

export.definition: to send goods to another country
export.definition_zh: 出口；把货物运往另一个国家

interrupt.definition: to break into a conversation or activity

eruption.definition: a sudden outburst (of a volcano or a rash)
eruption.definition_zh: 喷发；突然爆发，如火山喷发或出疹

predict.definition_zh: 预测；说出将要发生的事

postscript.definition: a note added after the signature (P.S.)
postscript.definition_zh: 附言；签名之后补充的文字（P.S.）

circumnavigate.definition: to sail all the way around

conductor.literal_zh: 把人带到一起的引导者
conductor.definition: a person who directs an orchestra; something that carries heat or electricity
conductor.definition_zh: 指挥；导体，即传导热或电的物质

abduct.definition: to take someone away by force

projectile.definition: an object that is thrown or fired
projectile.definition_zh: 抛射物；被投掷或发射出去的物体

dissect.definition: to cut open in order to study

bisect.definition: to divide into two equal parts

insecticide.literal_zh: 杀死身体分节的生物之物
insecticide.definition_zh: 杀虫剂；杀死昆虫的化学物质

genocide.definition: the deliberate destruction of a whole people
genocide.definition_zh: 种族灭绝；蓄意毁灭一个民族或族群

monotheism.definition: belief that there is only one God
monotheism.definition_zh: 一神论；相信只有一位神

atheist.definition: a person who believes no god exists
atheist.definition_zh: 无神论者；认为神不存在的人

polygon.definition: a flat shape with three or more straight sides
polygon.definition_zh: 多边形；由三条或更多直边围成的平面图形

octopus.definition: a sea animal with eight arms
